terminal_record.title: Internal Draft — Unverified Tariff and Price Allegations
terminal_record.description_short: The supplied record alleges a 6% tariff-related price rise and attempted data suppression; its CPI contradiction and unsupported effects remain unresolved.
terminal_record.description_medium: The frozen record alleges prices rose 6% by late August 2025 after tariffs, households lost savings, and officials tried to suppress data. A prior review disputes the 6% figure, citing August CPI readings of 0.4% month over month and 2.9% year over year, but supplies no source URLs or excerpts. These claims remain unverified; no causal, household-harm, or suppression finding is established.
terminal_record.description_long: The supplied entry places its allegation on August 26, 2025, and says consumer prices had risen 6% over a short period after new tariffs. It also claims those costs erased savings for middle- and working-class households and that the administration tried to suppress the related economic release. The packet does not include the underlying release, measurement series, tariff-price analysis, household data, or a document showing an attempted suppression; these statements therefore remain allegations in an internal draft. A prior review included in the packet disputes the aggregate 6% figure, citing August CPI readings of 0.4% month over month and 2.9% year over year, but the review supplies no source URL or excerpt here and was not independently rechecked in this reconciliation. Those figures do not establish what period, measure, or price change the frozen claim intended. This draft preserves the supplied allegation only to identify what remains unresolved: whether the 6% refers to CPI or another measure, what window it covers, whether tariff pass-through is established, and whether the asserted household effect and release-suppression allegation have supporting evidence. It does not conclude that prices surged, tariffs caused a particular increase, families lost savings, or officials suppressed data. The date remains copied from the frozen row and unverified.

terminal_record.title: Bondi Calls for DOJ Working Group to Review Trump and Jan. 6 Cases
terminal_record.description_short: AP reported that after her February 5 swearing-in, Bondi called for a DOJ group to review Trump and Jan. 6 prosecutions.
terminal_record.description_medium: The Associated Press reported that Pam Bondi was sworn in as attorney general on February 5, 2025, and hours later called for a Justice Department “weaponization working group.” AP said the group would scrutinize Jack Smith’s work and review prosecutions stemming from January 6. The report documents a review directive, not a January 20 order to dismiss cases against Trump allies.
terminal_record.description_long: On February 5, 2025, the Associated Press reported that Pam Bondi was sworn in as attorney general and, hours later, called for a Justice Department “weaponization working group.” AP said the group would scrutinize the work of special counsel Jack Smith, who had charged Donald Trump in two criminal cases, and review what Bondi described as “unethical prosecutions” stemming from the January 6, 2021 attack on the Capitol. The supplied original entry instead claimed that Bondi ordered DOJ to drop or suspend a broad set of cases against Trump allies on January 20, including fraud and campaign-finance matters. The date is incompatible with AP’s account of Bondi taking office on February 5, and the AP article describes reviews rather than case dismissals. This correction records the same-day directive AP documents and does not claim that cases were dismissed. It also does not treat the act of reviewing cases as proof of misconduct. The record does not establish which cases, if any, the working group later recommended for action or what outcomes followed.
